stories.head: True Anomaly's $190M Series C raises eyebrows
stories.body: True Anomaly has secured a $190 million Series C funding round, pushing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The company specializes in co-orbital security and space domain awareness, indicating a strong pull from the Department of Defense. This funding underscores the growing emphasis on securing space assets, as the military increasingly views space as a contested domain.
stories.soWhat: Investors are clearly betting that the future of warfare will play out in orbit, making True Anomaly a key player in a crowded field.

stories.head: Airbus capitalizes on satellite demand surge
stories.body: Airbus is taking advantage of the growing demand for satellite systems, reportedly ramping up production to meet the needs of both commercial and governmental clients. The company’s recent reorganization appears to be paying off, as it aligns with a market that’s projected to expand by nearly 10% annually over the next five years. This comes at a time when competitors are still figuring out their strategies.
stories.soWhat: Airbus's timing suggests they’re not just in the game; they’re playing to win, leaving others scrambling to catch up.

stories.head: Palantir extends TITAN program by $480M
stories.body: Palantir has received a $480 million extension on its TITAN ground station program, which is crucial for the Department of Defense's data management strategy. This extension highlights the government's ongoing commitment to data-driven decision-making in defense operations. With the Pentagon increasingly reliant on AI and data analytics, Palantir is firmly entrenched in the military’s tech ecosystem.
stories.soWhat: The extension is a reminder that in defense, data remains king, and Palantir is well-positioned to reign.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
